numbers: introductory-statistics-2e 의 200섹션 중 도표·데이터 표제가 33섹션(16.5%) [측정: TOC 표제 정규식].
그중 하나(2.1 Stem-and-Leaf Graphs …)를 실제로 읽으니 산문 문단 8개 중 도표를 말로 설명하는 문단은 1개(39어)뿐이고, 나머지는 작도 절차 지시와 연습문제용 수치 나열이다 [측정: 본문 판독].
같은 섹션의 정제 잔존율 62.4% · 6~40어 문장 비율 37.2% — 표본 10개 중 최저다(다른 9개는 69.6~94.9%) [측정].
B_slot_check.conclusion: 기출 「도표」 유형은 자료를 **읽어 주는** 산문이고, 통계 교과서는 자료를 **만드는 법**을 가르치는 절차문이다. 표제로 세면 33섹션이지만 슬롯을 채우는 것은 문단 단위로 극소수다.

A_style_mismatch.finding: 철학 69.2% · 경제 69.2% · 작문 75% · 생물 80% 는 A 대역에 든다. 그러나 정치 0% · 세계사 27.8% · 사회학 30% · 인류학 31.3% 는 A 대역 밖이고, 고유명사 밀도가 6.03~8.66/100어로 오히려 **B 대역(2.26~15.63)** 에 든다 [측정].

cases.before: One of the ways to respond to cognitive biases is to develop good habits of mind. There are no quick fixes or easy solutions to cognitive biases. Remember, these biases are a result of the way the brain works. Nevertheless, metacognition and critical reflection, as well as good mental habits, can help combat these natural tendencies in thought that otherwise leads us astray. The strategies outlined below can help you become a better philosopher. You should compare them with the methods philosophers use to arrive at truth, covered in Chapter 1.
cases.after: Cognitive bias has no quick fix. A bias is not a lapse of effort but a by-product of the way the mind ordinarily works, which is why resolving to think harder does not dislodge one. What can be built instead is a habit: the practice of watching a conclusion form, asking why it already feels obvious, and holding it open until the reasoning behind it has been stated aloud. Such a habit does not remove the tendency to reason badly. It makes the tendency visible early enough to be corrected, and that is a different and more modest kind of remedy.

cases.before: Hunter-gatherer cultures also built large structures, such as the monumental architecture at Göbekli Tepe in southeast Turkey and at Poverty Point in Louisiana in the United States. Listen to this TEDx Talk lecture by the archaeologist who excavated at Göbekli Tepe to find out more about the site. You can learn more about the Poverty Point culture by exploring the Poverty Point website. Look especially at “History and Artifacts.”
cases.after: Hunter-gatherers also built on a monumental scale. At one upland site in the ancient Near East, and at another beside a river in North America, people who did not farm raised stone enclosures and earthworks that must have taken many hands and many seasons to finish. Work of that size is usually read as evidence of settled life, since a population has to stay in one place long enough to finish it. These builders did not stay. They moved with the seasons and returned, which means the monument came before the village rather than after it.

B_slot_check.question: 실용문·데이터 기술이 B 무리(가중치 1.00)를 채우는가?
findings: foodsafety(CC BY · 14,526어 · 10장)는 절차·주의사항·작업지시로 된 **실용문**이다. 표본 장에서 40어 이상 산문 문단이 27개 나왔다 — 표본 20개 중 두 번째로 많다 [측정].
⚠️ 그러나 문체가 B 기준과 어긋난다: 고유명사 0.96/100어(B 기준 2.26~15.63) · 0개인 문단 85.2%(B 기준 0~17%) · 문단 어수 중앙 59(B 기준 91~136) [측정]. 사람·기관 이름이 없는 실용문이기 때문이다.
introductorybusinessstatistics(CC BY)의 표본 장에서 수치를 말로 기술하는 문단이 43개 중 11개(25.6%)다 — OpenStax 통계(8개 중 4개, 그러나 전부 작도 예제)와 달리 서술 비중이 있다 [측정].
B_slot_check.conclusion: B 슬롯은 **갈래로는 있고 문체로는 미달**이다. 기출 B 무리(안내문·내용일치)의 고유명사 밀도는 사람·기관 이름에서 오는데, 교과서 실용문에는 그 이름이 없다. 문체를 맞추려면 가공에서 이름을 **넣어야** 한다 — 확보가 아니라 창작이다.

cases.after: A large cut of meat does not cool properly, even in a cold room built for the purpose, and neither does a whole bird. A pot of soup of four litres or more can take a day or longer to fall to four degrees. Depth is the reason. Heat leaves a dense mass only through its surface, so the centre stays warm long after the outside feels cold, and the hours in between are exactly the hours in which bacteria multiply. The remedy follows from the cause: divide the food, spread it shallow, and the same fridge that failed will cool it in an hour.
cases.note: 전방참조는 원문 뒤 9항 목록의 1항(shallow pans)을 읽어 해소했다 — 문단 하나만으로는 풀리지 않았다.

cases.before: We will discuss Simmel’s formal sociology later in the chapter. In general, the solution to the question — How is society possible? — differs depending on the level of analysis used to pose the question. Excluding the global for the time being (see Chapter 1. An Introduction to Sociology), sociologists describe group behaviour at three levels of social interaction: micro, meso, and macro.
cases.after: What holds a society together has no single answer, because the answer changes with the scale at which the question is asked. Ask it of two people talking and it turns on how they take turns and read each other’s signals. Ask it of a workplace or a congregation and it turns on how many separate roles are kept in step at once. Ask it of a whole country and it turns on institutions that outlast everyone inside them. Sociologists work at all three scales and treat them as different questions rather than rival answers.
cases.note: 세 층위의 내용은 같은 절의 뒤 두 문단(micro · meso 설명)에서 끌어왔다 — 문단 하나만으로는 「micro/meso/macro」라는 이름표만 남는다.
